name: Nexkin Adaptive Undershirt
description:
A form-fitting crew-neck undershirt from Nexkin — a Tier 3/4 technical apparel label — made from a proprietary stretch-weave fabric embedded with a passive thermal regulation mesh. The mesh doesn't require power; it's a phase-change material woven directly into the fabric that absorbs heat when the wearer runs hot and releases it when they cool down. The effect is subtle and real: not air conditioning, not heating, just a persistent effort to keep the wearer somewhere near comfortable. The shirt itself is seamless at the shoulders and sides, with flat-locked seams everywhere else.

It's designed to be worn under other garments and is almost aggressively uninteresting to look at — available in black, white, and a medium grey. The value is entirely in the wear. Tier 3 office workers, people with augments that run hot, and anyone who spends long hours in climate-inconsistent environments (construction, field work, transit) wear these as a quiet investment in their own comfort. Some Tier 4 professionals wear them under suits without mentioning it.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation via phase-change material mesh — no power required. Absorbs excess body heat and releases it gradually to maintain consistent skin-surface temperature. Effective range approximately ±4°C from baseline comfort.
what_it_says: You've solved problems other people don't bother to think about. Practical investment in invisible comfort — the kind of person who optimizes without making a show of it.
worn_by: office workers with augments that run hot
story_hooks: A batch of Nexkin undershirts from late 2199 has a phase-change material that was slightly overformulated — under extreme stress conditions (high-intensity physical exertion in hot environments), the mesh can release heat too quickly, causing localized surface burns.
Someone has been stealing Nexkin undershirts specifically — not for resale, but apparently for the phase-change material itself, which has an unrelated industrial application someone has figured out.
A character's Nexkin undershirt malfunctions during a high-stakes situation, its thermal regulation kicking in at exactly the wrong moment and masking a fever they needed to be aware of.
